songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Epic The Other One → Turn On Your Lovelight jam with Peter Green
ai_show_review.blurb: The show features a monster The Other One into an extended Turn On Your Lovelight with guest guitarist Peter Green. Jerry’s tone shines on China Cat Sunflower and the Cold Rain outro, while Phil’s bass becomes clearer after the early mix settles. The second half delivers tight jams despite a muddy opening.
ai_show_review.review: On February 1, 1970 at New Orleans’ Warehouse the Dead delivered a historic set that still feels fresh for listeners today. After an uneven start – the soundboard mixes Bob Weir too high and drums low in the first few tunes – the band settles into a deep groove. The highlight is undoubtedly the marathon jam from The Other One straight into Turn On Your Lovelight, where guest legend Peter Green trades fiery licks with Jerry Garcia, whose tone is described as “perfect” throughout. Earlier in the set, the classic China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue sparkles, and a haunting Cold Rain And Snow guitar outro showcases Garcia’s lyrical phrasing. Phil Lesh adds a brief Dark Star spark before his bass cuts through more clearly later, while Pigpen’s vocals and organ sit nicely once the mix stabilizes. Drummers Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann emerge from the early low‑level muddle to provide solid, if occasionally long‑winded, rhythmic support. Overall, despite the rough opening, the performance is a gritty yet compelling snapshot of the Dead in ’70, highlighted by one of the most memorable Lovelight jams of the era.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard capture after the early roughness; balances Pigpen’s vocals, clearly captures Peter Green guest solo and overall band dynamics.

key_highlights: The Other One → Turn On Your Lovelight extended jam with guest Peter Green
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider segue shines with bright Jerry tone
Cold Rain And Snow guitar outro showcases Garcia’s phrasing
High Time delivers solid groove despite early mix issues

band_performance.Jerry: Trades licks with guest Peter Green on the Lovelight jam; tone praised as perfect, especially on China Cat Sunflower and the Cold Rain guitar outro.
band_performance.Phil: Adds a brief Dark Star spark; bass becomes clearer and more present after the early mix settles.
band_performance.Bob: Mix is too forward at the start but provides solid rhythm work throughout the set.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are low/inaudible in the opening, then become audible and provide steady support despite a slightly long‑winded segment.
band_performance.Billy: Shares the drum duties with Mickey; early mix issues improve later, delivering solid rhythmic foundation.
